$description: Artifacts-only extension tokens: the 'memory domain' violet accent (art-violet-*) plus the workspace browse-shell constants (art-panel-*, art-browser-band-height). The violet source is artifacts/static/css/gallery.css lines 34-38 (dark) and 161-164 (light) — a decorative brand accent (not body text). The high-contrast family AUTHORS its own groups rather than inheriting: that family is fully monochrome, and an inherited violet would be the one hue left on the page — so art-violet resolves to the achromatic mono ramp there, keeping the memory domain's visual separation as a lightness step instead of a hue. The art-panel-*/art-browser-band-height group is the stacked two-card browse shell (a compact browser band above a dominant detail card): theme-independent layout constants, repeated identically in every group here (mirroring web_terminal.json's wt-header-height pattern).

art-panel-radius.$description: Grafana-style card corner radius for the browse-view cards and their in-card chrome (frame 2a). Theme-independent layout constant.

art-panel-gap.$description: Canvas gutter around and between the stacked browser band + detail cards (padding:8px;gap:8px workspace region). Theme-independent.

art-browser-band-height.$description: Height of the scrollable artifact-list strip in the browse-view browser band (the #sidebar-body list). Bounded so the detail card below stays dominant; the list scrolls within it. Theme-independent.

art-violet.$description: AUTHORED rather than inherited, for the same reason the high-contrast groups are: the `desy` family uses DESY Styleguide (06/24) hexes only, and an inherited #9f7aea would be the one off-palette hue on the page. The styleguide publishes its own Violet, so the memory domain keeps its violet identity rather than degrading to a lightness step. `light` collapses onto `base` — DESY publishes nothing lighter than Violet in this hue.

light.$description: Collapsed onto base: the palette has no lighter violet, and Purple (2.56:1) is darker.

dark.$description: DESY Purple — the deeper step of the pair.
